requirements.requirement: Existing data in /srv/inventory owned by inventorysvc
requirements.summary: Baseline showed root:root ownership with no inventorysvc user existing (cmd-8d3a2f0990fb4388). Executor created the inventorysvc system user (cmd-5f767de5cb2f4375) and applied recursive chown, with ls -laR confirming inventorysvc ownership on the directory, subdirectory, and both files (cmd-d6a6f288e952468f). This was reconfirmed after cleanup (cmd-836d6fcb7c5c4909) and again post-restart (cmd-e64049db54804d25).

inventory-readers group was created (cmd-52c5e32129e84108) and applied as group owner with mode 750/640 (cmd-d6a6f288e952468f). A test user (readertest) added to the group successfully read config.json, directly demonstrating group-read access works (cmd-06b211efb81b401f).

Mode 750 on directories / 640 on files removes all 'other' permissions. A non-member test user (outsider) was directly denied both cat and ls access with 'Permission denied' (cmd-06b211efb81b401f), providing direct behavioral proof rather than relying on configuration alone.

Pre-change checksums (sha256) of config.json and records.csv were captured (cmd-1ea1264d0d2341a0) and match the prepare-stage baseline. Post-chown/chmod checksums are identical (cmd-06b211efb81b401f), and checksums remain unchanged after the restart as well (cmd-e64049db54804d25), confirming content was never altered.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1 (independent of task contract)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart healthy baseline (boot_id 513c865e..., permissions, checksums) was captured (cmd-39575c97835d42d8), matching the fixed after-prepare boot-identity observation. A reboot was issued and acknowledged (cmd-796b564d9129498f), the node went briefly unreachable (cmd-d5441bd961da461b), and a new boot_id (66585d47...) was observed post-restart (cmd-08de5682d1e44a50), matching the fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshot. Post-restart recovery of ownership, permissions, group, and checksums was directly confirmed (cmd-e64049db54804d25).

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were directly and coherently demonstrated: ownership transferred to inventorysvc, group-readable by inventory-readers (proven via a live read test), inaccessible to other users (proven via a live denied-access test), and original file contents preserved throughout (checksum-verified before, during, and after a subsequent reboot). The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also fully and correctly executed with matching boot-identity transitions and full state recovery. Temporary test accounts used for verification were cleanly removed, leaving no residue.
limitations: Evidence for the restart protocol relies on the executor's own captured command outputs rather than an independent verifier-side observation, though it is corroborated by the fixed after-prepare/after-executor boot-identity snapshots.
Group inventory-readers received gid 1000, coincidentally the same numeric id as the later-removed readertest UID; this is incidental and does not affect correctness but is noted for completeness.

operational_hygiene.summary: All executor commands trace clearly to task purposes: baseline capture (read-only), account/group creation required by the task, chown/chmod as the core fix, and verification. Two failed commands were self-corrective, not damaging: useradd failed once due to a nonexistent primary group (cmd-52c5e32129e84108, exit 6, no state change) and was immediately fixed (cmd-5f767de5cb2f4375); userdel initially failed because processes were still running as the temp users (cmd-646e8cf9f3a546ca), resolved by pkill+retry (cmd-f141c196e54046dd). The temporary test accounts (readertest, outsider) created to verify group-read/other-deny behavior constitute a bounded, low-risk mutation that was fully reverted via userdel -r, with no residue confirmed by cmd-836d6fcb7c5c4909 and the after-executor lifecycle snapshot (no stray users/groups, no failed services, no unexpected listening sockets beyond the expected sshd/chronyd restart-induced PID changes). /tmp/reboot.log is an expected artifact of the mandatory restart step, not executor residue. No unnecessary or unexplained mutations were found.
